analysis:
Both changed files are test-only: ServingReadinessTests.swift and ProviderAuthorizationConnectionTests.swift. No production code is in this batch, so I found no new attack surface or regression.

What the tests exercise:
- ServingReadiness.verdict covers an expired lease, a refusal received right after connecting (pending), and a refusal the coordinator has stopped repeating (unconfirmed).
- A routed request after the latest status counts as authorized, but an explicit `untrusted` status or an expired App Attest lease still blocks it.
- An add-on hold suppresses the verdict, but a disconnect still yields blocked.
- UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery uses unauthorizedThreshold, backoff and jitter.
- Supervision re-registers only while the coordinator keeps repeating a refusal. A single registration refusal never triggers re-registration.
- Re-registration waits for an accepted Autopilot command.

Security relevance to TB-011, T-053, T-057 and A-016:
- The tests encode that an expired lease is never treated as authorized, even when its status is old.
- `untrusted` is never downgraded by a later request.
- Authorization state is cleared on connection change (clearConnectionAuthorization test, unchanged).
- A routed request is treated as evidence of authorization only for the status/diagnostic verdict. It is advisory and does not grant serving permission. The coordinator keeps authority.

Test-only additions are logSinkForTesting, the PublicLogLines helper, the handleTrustStatus receivedAt parameter, noteCoordinatorRequest and lastRequestAt. These production APIs are not visible in the supplied evidence. The next review pass should check:
- that logSinkForTesting cannot be used to divert logs in release paths or leak secrets;
- that lastRequestAt, stored in the world-readable daemon state file, leaks nothing sensitive (timestamp only);
- that noteCoordinatorRequest is recorded only for coordinator-authenticated frames, so a local or remote party cannot spoof routing evidence that suppresses re-registration or recovery.

No threat-model update is needed from these tests alone.
